terms: (phase == D1) * table(prev_action*10 + prev_state*2 + prev_reward, {13: -0.1, 12: 0.13, 15: -0.37, 14: -0.07, 25: -0.04, 24: 0.14, 23: 0.18, 22: 0.29}) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state",-2)==2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (tv("state",-1)==1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1)
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 10: timing dominates (D1 ~+0.6, GO ~+0.94, D2 ~-0.88; timing R^2 0.98). Beyond timing the main driver is the previous trial at D1: lowest after a1->S2 rewarded (-0.37), lower after a1->S1 rewarded, highest after a2->S1 unrewarded (+0.29), a2->S1 rewarded, a2->S2 / a1->S1 unrewarded (+0.13..+0.18); i.e. it codes last choice x state x reward (not a clean model-based repeat/switch axis). D1 is also raised (~+0.09) if the state two trials back was S2. At GO it is slightly higher after a reward (+0.07). At D2 it is less negative when the reached state is S1 (+0.14) and after choosing a1 (+0.05), slightly lower if the last trial reached S1 or was rewarded. Policy |logit| at GO, value, consecutive losses, hidden good state add ~nothing. Unexplained: occasional large GO drops (to ~0) in late-episode runs of unrewarded a2 trials. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.67 (dev 0.68) vs all ceiling 0.81, all-observed 0.78; all terms observed.

issues: The D1 claims hold. The residual-by-previous-trial table matches the stated codes: a1 S2 r -0.366, a2 S1 u +0.293, a2 S1 r +0.177, a2 S2 u +0.144, a1 S1 u +0.131, a1 S1 r -0.106. The fitted weight on the table term is 0.94. The tv('state',-2)==S2 weight is +0.088 and the GO prev_reward weight is +0.069, both as stated. Test R^2 0.666 reproduces.

The D2 description is an additive simplification that misdescribes the shape. The residual by this choice x state at D2 is a1S1 +0.136, a1S2 -0.081, a2S1 +0.024, a2S2 -0.101. So the 'S1 boost' is almost all a1->S1 common, and 'after choosing a1 (+0.05)' is wrong for a1->S2, which sits about where a2->S2 does. Replacing the additive D2 terms with (state==S1)*(action==1), (state==S1)*(prev_reward==1) and (action==prev_action) raises test R^2 from 0.666 to 0.714.

The S1 boost at D2 interacts with the previous reward. Adding (phase==D2)*(state==S1)*(prev_reward==1) alone raises test R^2 from 0.666 to 0.699, with weight +0.068. So the claim 'slightly lower when the previous trial was rewarded' (weight -0.019) has the sign wrong for S1 trials. It only holds as an additive average.
A small missed term: the first trial in the window (prev_action==-1) at D1 is under-predicted (+0.036). Adding it gives 0.675.

The large GO drops during runs of unrewarded a2 trials are acknowledged as unexplained. Run-length, |choice|, choice and GO previous-trial-table terms each add at most 0.001, so they stay rare and unexplained.
With better terms a gap remains: 0.71 against an observed-only ceiling of 0.78. The remaining misses are scattered by phase x previous trial (|error| <= 0.045), with no single large class.
